newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius index slips for first time in 3 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius index slips for first time in 3 weeks.

text.p: The Semdex market index at the Stock Exchange of Mauritius (SEM) eased 1.12 points to 327.56 on Friday ending eight consecutive sessions of upward trading.
Volume transacted rose to 19.70 million rupees on 769,694 shares from 6.13 million rupees on 293,319 shares on Wednesday.
The Semdex began to rise on October 25 after Mauritian Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam announced the setting up of a country fund that will invest 300 million rupees in the bourse next year.
In the process, the index was lifted from its year low of 305.41 points on October 23, gaining 7.6 percent in eight sessions until Wednesday.
The bourse official market trades on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
Brokers said falling stocks of two leading companies on Friday dragged the Semdex down, offsetting rising share prices of smaller companies.

"Most other shares in the rest of the list are still rising although at a relatively slower pace than during the past two weeks. The positive sentiment is still here and it's rather Air Mauritius and State Bank which dragged down the Semdex," one broker said.

National carrier Air Mauritius fell by 2 rupees to 52 on 12,875 shares after an announcement that its chairman and managing director Sir Harry Tirvengadum will join multinational airline Air Afrique in 1997.
State Bank was quoted ex-dividend on Friday at 8.50 rupees, down 20 cents on 174,900 shares. State Bank paid a final dividend of 20 cents per share for the financial year ended 30 June 1996.
Other leading shares on the market were mostly stable.
Mauritius Commercial Bank was stable at 73 rupees on 14,323 shares and Mauritius Oil Refineries remained at 9.50 rupees on 32,623 shares.
In the investment sector, Consolidated Investment Trust (CIT) fell by 30 cents to 9 rupees on 1,250 shares and Promotion And Development (PAD) edged up by 10 cents to 15.50 rupees on 9,000 shares.
Sugar stock Mon Tresor Mon Desert gained 20 cents to 37.40 rupees on 6,445 shares. Happy World Foods climbed 60 cents to to 16 rupees on 5,806 shares.
Conglomerates Rogers was unchanged at 90.50 rupees on 21,903 shares and Ireland Blyth added 30 cents to 13.60 rupees on 1,870 shares.
Hotel stocks Sun Resorts was unchanged at 36 rupees on 11,510 shares and New Mauritius Hotels remained at 29.50 rupees on a heavy 411,796 shares.
